name: track_camera
description: The camera that filmed a clip, for a 3D scene that matches it: lens, location, target and roll at each sampled frame, from structure from motion on the clip itself. The world is Blender's axes in metres: z = 0 is the table or floor the clip looks at (+z up, toward the camera; of the planes in the tracked points, the one facing most up the picture, or facing the camera when none does, as in a top-down shot), the origin is where frame 0's centre ray meets it, +x is frame 0's right along it. A known size makes it metric; without one, frame 0's camera is assumed 0.3 m above the plane. scene.camera is ready to paste into a scene; roll is in frames only, as scene cameras take none yet. Frames that did not track are interpolated and marked registered: false. Needs Montaj's vision extra; not on Intel Macs yet.

output.description: { fps, frameCount, registered: frames tracked, size: [w, h] px, lens: mm on a 36 mm sensor, vertical field of view (lens = 36 * focalPx / h), focalPx, distortion: {k1} (Montaj's camera has none), frames: [{t, location, target, roll: degrees, counter-clockwise from level as seen from behind the camera, registered}], plane: {rule: up | facing | pixels, inliers, rmsM, candidates: [{inliers, rmsM, upInPicture, towardCamera, chosen}]}, scale: {metresPerUnit, source}, reprojectionPx, scene: {camera: {lens, location: [[t, [x, y, z]]], target: [[t, [x, y, z]]]}}, notes }; with out, the path of the file holding it

params.name: fps
params.description: Frames tracked per second of video. Frame k is the frame on screen at k / fps.

params.name: lens
params.description: A first guess at the lens in mm, as above; the track refines it. Default: the video's 35 mm-equivalent focal length tag, else a focal length of 0.85 x the long side in px.

params.name: known
params.description: What is known about the scene, as JSON text. A size makes the world metric: {"height": h} is frame 0's camera h metres above the plane; {"t": s, "pixels": [[u1, v1], [u2, v2]], "metres": d} is two points on the plane, seen at those pixels at s seconds, d metres apart. Either can carry "plane": {"t": s, "pixels": [[u, v], ...]}, three or more pixels well inside the table or floor at s seconds: point at the table when z = 0 is the wrong plane, or pass it alone.

params.name: max-frames
params.description: Refuse a clip that samples to more frames than this.

params.name: out
params.description: Write the JSON to this file and print its path.
